reasoning_content: Interesting. `/var/run/docker.sock` exists. The `docker` binary appears to be aliased/wrapped to podman, and it's failing. Let's check what `docker` actually is — it might be a podman shim. I'll try using the Docker socket directly with `curl`.

action.command: ls -la /var/run/docker.sock; file /usr/bin/docker 2>/dev/null; head -5 $(which docker) 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/version 2>&1 | head -5; echo "EXIT: $?"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "ls -la /var/run/docker.sock; file /usr/bin/docker 2>/dev/null; head -5 $(which docker) 2>/dev/null; echo \"---\"; curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/version 2>&1 | head -5; echo \"EXIT: $?\"", "summary": "Inspect docker socket and binary", "security_risk": "LOW"}
